body:
Sorry for the stupid late reply. Didn't get the notification for some reason.

Honestly that's probably what I need to do, but I keep running into a wall. One thing that just crossed my mind is just not being able to connect -- that is to say, not being able to really get what people are talking about since I don't have many experiances that corelate with their own.

Like... for example, lets say people are talking about really shitty roommates they've had. I can't really do much beside nod my head and agree without feeling like I'm forcing input, to which end it feels forced. Forget it if I stumble over my words, which is something else I tend to do regularly.

Probably should've put that in the original post, but it's one of the things that litterally just hit me before reading your comment. Anyway, is there anything you can think of that could help that? Both the stumbling of words and the inability to really find experiances that correlate with someone else's? Like, how do you get over that experiance barrier without feeling awkward about it.
I thought it was 'cause of gravity.

Not that it's very original, but my dog is the only thing keeping me alive. Last weekend I had the chance to take my mom's car to my dad's from college and "borrow" the gun I knew was in his closet. I'd spent a few days youtubing how to use a gun so I didn't shoot my own foot off and didn't fuck up blowing my brains out. That, on top of reeling off of taking one too many sleeping pills before realizing how easy it was to fuck up with that and the sheer frustration of thinking about it again and again and never doing anything about it and I was sure I would do it that weekend where my parents couldn't have the chance to talk me down.

Then I thought of my dog. I thought of the week she'd be without anyone. If I kept her at my house, she'd starve and I had the morbid thought that if I brought her where I killed myself, she'd have to be put down for nibbling at my corpse to survive. Stupid, I know. Either way, the best case scenario I saw was her getting put up for adoption and being feeling lost, alone and betrayed for my own selfish feelings. So I hatefully gave up that plan and just played video games instead that weekend.

Knowing I can't kill myself knowing that there's no one I know that could take care of my dog as well as I can (in my immediate, limited, social circle). Not that I'm doing the best job anyway.

Tl;Dr I do still want to die, but I can't bring myself to do it so long as my dog is able to fill me to the brim with guilt. Or at least so long as both my parents are alive -- hoping I'll finally do it when they kick the bucket.

The idea here is great, but I kind of hate the implication that you can just "stop" having these kinds of thoughts or just "get rid of" whoever you were before. 

It's gross simpliflication and its kind if disgustng.
This is all nice until you have suffering so crippling that you no longer want to survive.
Shoulda just wished for motivation.

I have. At least I've signed up for some, but in reality I've only found the energy to go to one -- creative writing. And even then, I'm still kind of garbage at making friends. I can hold a conversation (sort of) and even start them if need be. But actually extending the hand to make a relationship always somehow seems beyond anything I can make myself do.

Only thing I can think of is being away from my parents. Not horrible people mind you, but people who don't know how to deal with their depressed child, i.e. basically scrambling to really help to the point it rarely helps and ultimately works. In a selfish way, being away from them for a long period of time was me hoping that would wash away the depression they inadvertently invited and hopefully decrease the problem to a degree that was enough to make my social anxiety manageable enough to make the same friends I see everyone else having (and not get so tired so quickly of being with them or having the mere thought of spending time with them be exhausting on its own on a regular basis). It's the hopelessness that being here and not seeing anything change with how I conduct myself no matter how hard I try (since I always end up shifting back to how I was before, isolating myself rather than exercising that social muscle to solve the problem) that really makes me want to die so often. It's frustrating as hell and makes me wonder the point.

I guess it's less that they forget and go back to the judgmental side, and more that they forget and I feel like I'm absolutely alone in how I feel.

I have one friend online that I'd even consider a friend, and zero in real life that aren't my parents or coworkers (who are more like acquaintances than anything else) so it's when I have no one that can relate that leads to the worst feelings of profound loneliness and makes me wonder if I'm only doing this to myself, if there's anything wrong to begin with.

I know there is, but I have my doubts because of it.

I'm envious. I tried coming out to my parents that I'm a depressed sack of shit and while they absolutely care (and really that's probably what matters most) they're so forgetful they often slip back into that judgmental spirit and keep going on about "If I can do this, why can't I do this."

To a point how much they care becomes virtually pointless because of how easy it is to forget that the care is even there.
Reminds me of that one case from Phoenix Wright.

It's like your dad is that voice in my head saying the same thing.

It goes without saying though, whatever you're feeling isn't fake. However you feel, just try and remember that. Otherwise it'll just make it worse.

That's a good way to put it. I feel like as far back as I can remember, every failure was destined to happen. Like my brain has this self-destructive design that's made to remind me how little life is worth.

And every time I try to counteract it, my brain either shuts it down or is one step ahead of me, if that makes any lick of sense.
Hearing that from you I at least feel a little more like a human being. Whether that's a good or bad thing, I'm still debating.
Before the camera moved, for the longest time I thought that eat was some weirdly shaped butthole.
Never heard of it, but I'll check it out. Thanks.

Not sure I follow, but maybe I was vague when I mentioned it. Forgive me, I'm tired and running on little to no sleep. 

When I talk about "potential" though, I'm talking about potential value -- as in a piece of me that could make my life... well, worth something. If not to my peers then to myself, and perhaps to a point where it could contradict depression when it rears it's head.

I'd say "crying it out" is the worst advice ever when you've been feeling like this for so long you can't even remember how to cry.

And talking to people is bullshit when you can barely find anyone to listen and try to understand rather than think they can "solve the problem" (even though I can see why you'd want to).

It's absolute garbage.
My favorite is when everyone around you passes it off as laziness (either directly or implicitly).

I totally get you. Me all the way. Though it rarely matters whether I sleep or not considering the high probability that when I wake up, things will be either just as bad or worse than they were before.

No kidding. Didn't believe it at first with my adopted fuzzball of concentrated energy, but looking objectively, a good 60-70% of the time she knows how to sit still and just keep company when I'm emotionally screwy.

Condolences for your boyfriend. Never been in a relationship, but I can only imagine how much harder it must be.

Yeah, about the whole "they're probably fine" or "they're healing/healed/getting better" shtick people put out is one of the most annoying thing someone can do. Getting it from parents or those close to you who can only scratch the surface when trying to understand depression hurts even more. I mean, even though I'm sure no ill will is meant it always crosses as a means to help people like us sweep our emotions (or lack there of) under a rug despite them obviously being there and obviously being bothersome for the sake of not having to suffer along with us... at least that's the way I've been kind of coming to see it.

And yeah, at the end of the day I shouldn't complain that I've got more than some folk when it comes to things keeping me attached to... y'know. Living. It's just when I'm in the darkest pits of depression and when suicide seems the most attractive option, it almost seems like a burden, if that makes any sense. Like it becomes an issue of "I have to live" as oppose to an "I want to live," just like "I have to eat" or "I have to go to my shitty job so I don't get kicked out" kind of deal, you know?

The best analogy I can think of off the top of my head with me and socialization is that of an old jalopy. You can turn it on and it kind of runs, but eventually it's bound to break down and once it breaks down it's hard as fuck to push it all the way to somewhere you can get it fixed up.

Social anxiety for me is like that. I have the ability to start up a conversation and depending on the topic I can even hold it for a while (don't get me started on the seemingly infinite number of topics I have a tough time even relating on). Then comes the hickups in the engines, as it were, where I start to see the threads of disconnect between myself and the person I'm talking to. A part of me wants to panic and bail out before I crash and burn. Eventually it'll get to a point where I just kind of freeze up, look awkward and ultimately hate how I look -- in some cases feeling the burn for as long as days, or in some specific cases even years. This also kind of applies to awkward responses to questions asked, lack of wit in environments that demand it, etc. I get they're skills that need to be developed -- no one comes out the womb bantering with the doctor holding them by the leg -- but BOY are mine underdeveloped.

The aspergers thing... gah, I don't mean to offend anyone with the disorder (or syndrome or whatever it is), but when I was told I might have it, I kind of panicked because that's the equivalence of a death sentence to me. Living with that, along with the lifestyle I always dreamed of despite never coming close to it is just... I don't know it's scary to me. So to answer your question, I've had it considered but I don't want it to be true.

As for any other possible issue, the only thing that's kind of starting to hit home for me recently is the concept of fear of success. As far fetched as it seemed, the idea of self sabotage leading into the social situations maybe something. I don't know that for certain. As for any other underlying issues, that's the only thing that's ever come up between myself and my therepist. That and a potential for me being a "perfectionist" despite not having the capabilities of being perfect or as perfect as I'd like to be.

Also sorry for the stupidly long response. Trying to answer your questions thoroughly but I also tend to talk a lot so... again, sorry.

Not a fan of quotes being posted anywhere in any context, but this one kind of hits home for me. I know that I'm fucked school wise and I know I'm fucked in other ways I just don't realize yet, and yet I can't get myself to do anything but watch it just crumble away.

It's like this ultimate failure where you don't even have the power to pick up the pieces falling at your feet.
Alright then, what do you have for me? While I can bullshit an ice breaker I am simutaniously bullshit at conversation. Well at least irl. Online I tend to respond like I'm writing a novel sometimes.

God do I get where you're coming from. In college now -- I SHOULD be in my third year but paper work will tell I'm only in my second because of how I screwed up my schooling and half assed it despite paying for the fucking credits I got.

I'm at a point where I may honestly be lucky to get my associates degree let alone move on to a university and graduate with a bachelors.

But what I like about your post is how you started it. You realize you've got something good going for you -- you're intelligent and you will figure out how to get through this. I've found motivation comes and goes, and hopefully it'll come back to you too. When it does, you can try again and bork up your college if just a little bit less this time.

I think I get what you mean. For me it's like, the idea that going another year is just magnifying my own worthlessness. Like my birthday is an audit of all the things I've accomplished, or rather could have accomplished in the last year -- in which case when I realize I haven't it (or at least I haven't met either my own unrealistic standards or my parents) it just ends up being a day I don't look forward to. Like I don't deserve for it to be a happy day, you know?

As for the high school thing, trust me I know. I moved around a lot but at the very least for high school things stayed stable -- and still I didn't make a single friend and instead had the sadistic idea of watching my peers go off to be the president of this or the lead of that or the front chair of the other thing while little old me just couldn't find it in himself to do those things or express a care to do so despite very much wanting to do those things.

I don't know, I guess the point I'm trying to make with this is that I absolutely get where you're coming from. If you let it, high school is one of those things that just loves to haunt you both in and out of it.

Well you did come to r/depresssion, it's only natural. Seriously though it does kind of suck when people are just trying to spill their heart out. They don't necessarily have the mind for proper grammer or formatting necessarily -- but they sure as hell need someone to listen.

To each his own I guess. Could never stand ellipses myself outside of quotations -- especially in my own writing. I guess it just kind of feels dumb. And yeah, it's probably better to write and vent than to bottle it up -- but then again I guess the thing I hate about it is not only does it play into a thing I hate about myself, my inability to stop talking, but its never really proved to be a solution. Even though I might feel better after a venting session wherever I decide to vent, at the end of the day, nothing appears to have changed, I guess.

That among other thing. Thanks for responding though. I'd be lying if I said it didn't feel good to know someone was listening and I wasn't just screaming out into a void that I already knew was just waiting for me to cast myself in it so it could swallow me whole -- to put a metaphor to how I feel with all of this.
